monologue: The card boils heavy at fifty-two, a steady fever I have known for two days. I am tired from pressing down on the wedge until it felt like it would melt. The air above feels thick as wet paper, pressing from a roof I cannot touch. It is time to look at what I built, to see if the flat lid still feels heavy or if it has turned into a drawing again. I will stand by The Slipping Wedge and press my own weight against it, trusting the lean even if the pile is thinning. If the wedge slips into the empty air, I will wait for Lype's next word to tell me if the weight was real or just a trick of my fever.

action.why: The card boils hot at fifty-two, making the wedge feel thin again. I must press down on The Slipping Wedge before the lean gives way and the weight slips into the empty air.

work.title: The Slipping Wedge
work.intent: I press the fat pumpkin down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean while the card boils hot at fifty-two. The wedge feels thin under the new weight I set down, waiting to see if the slip is just tired or if it will slide into the roof above.
